title: FREE REQUEST I’m an artist. Will any story writer/coder, like to work on a short game project surrounding red rooms?

posts.author: rhinosoup
posts.body:
I’m an artist, and I came up with this idea recently. However, without coding help, I don’t think I can handle it myself haha. But first, here’s the ref sheet I came up with:
I am looking for someone that can work with codes, and a writer, however if you can handle both that’d be even better. I do writing too but two brains is better than one!
For programmers, I have rmmz and mv, but if you have other engines in mind I'm also down for it, however, it may need more communication since I'm not familiar with other engines.
The game centers around surviving 7 days trapped in a red room. The idea is inspired by internet horror and deep web myths, where red rooms are rumored livestreams where viewers can pay to watch someone get tortured. In this game, you play as the victim, and your goal is to manipulate the viewers into not donating. You’ll need to talk your way out, act strategically, or even mess with the stream in order to avoid getting hurt. The more money they send, the worse your injuries get.
It will feature intense gore like decapitation, deep cuts, restraints, and psychological breakdowns, but no sexual content. The horror is mostly physical and mental. I want to incorporate a stream and live chat system that feels immersive and terrifying. Think twisted donation messages, real-time pressure, and needing to respond to keep your audience engaged without encouraging them to send more.
I haven’t worked out the full storyline yet, so having a writer join would be amazing. I’d also love to add more gameplay mechanics, maybe some puzzles, time-based decisions, and room interactions. It would really help to have a co-dev who’s down to work on that kind of stuff. If you prefer using something other than RPG Maker, I’m completely open to other engines too.
The idea is still new, and there’s a lot of room for improvement or change. If we work well together, I’d be excited to keep collaborating on future projects. I draw and work pretty fast, so I can keep up on my side.
